First, we find the derivative of $f(t)$ by differentiating each component:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{5-2t})\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t))\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-3{t}^{4})\,k \\  & =-2{e}^{5-2t}\,i+3\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)\,j-12{t}^{3}\,k\end{aligned}
$$

  

Then, we calculate ${f}^{″}(t)$ by differentiating ${f}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-2{e}^{5-2t})\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t))\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-12{t}^{3})\,k \\  & =-2(-2{e}^{5-2t})\,i+3(-3\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t))\,j-12(3{t}^{2})\,k \\  & =4{e}^{5-2t}\,i-9\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)\,j-36{t}^{2}\,k\end{aligned}
$$
